repository.name: pm4py-core
repository.description: PM4Py is the leading open source process mining library in Python that supports state-of-the-art process mining algorithms for process discovery, conformance checking, and process enhancement
repository.organization: Process Intelligence Solutions (PIS), spin-off from Fraunhofer Institute FIT

license.type: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0
conditions: Include original license and copyright notices
Provide copy of license to recipients
Disclose source code to all users
CRITICAL: Provide source code to users interacting with the software remotely through a computer network (network copyleft clause - Section 13)
license.assessment: AGPL-3.0 is a strong copyleft license with network provision that requires derivative works to be open-sourced under AGPL-3.0, including when used as a network service. This makes it unsuitable for direct reuse in closed-source or proprietary products. The organization offers separate commercial licensing for closed-source use. For UML-Codex, algorithms and patterns can be studied and re-implemented, but code cannot be directly lifted without AGPL compliance.

algorithm_organization.description: Each algorithm provides a factory method as single access point with standardized input/output
benefits: Runtime algorithm selection via variant parameter
Easy to add new algorithm variants
algorithm_organization.implementation: apply() function in each algorithm module accepts variant enum to select implementation

algorithm_organization.description: Multiple algorithm implementations encapsulated as interchangeable strategies via Variants enum
benefits: Swap algorithms without changing client code
Add new strategies without modifying existing code
Easy A/B testing of different approaches
algorithm_organization.implementation: Variants enum defines available strategies, exec_utils.get_variant() selects implementation

algorithm_organization.description: Polymorphic input handling accepts multiple data types (EventLog, DataFrame, DFG) and adapts to internal format
benefits: No code duplication for different input types
algorithm_organization.implementation: Type checking with Union types, conversion to canonical format before processing
algorithm_organization.example: Inductive miner accepts EventLog, DataFrame, DFG, or UVCL and normalizes to UVCL

algorithm_organization.description: Base algorithm defines skeleton, specific variants override steps
algorithm_organization.implementation: apply() dispatches to apply_trace() or apply_log() based on input type

data_structures.description: Python properties encapsulate access to internal attributes with validation
Event implements Mapping protocol, Trace implements Sequence protocol
Petri net places and transitions use object identity rather than value equality
data_structures.rationale: Graph nodes must be distinct even if they have identical properties

data_structures.description: Custom __deepcopy__ methods with memo dictionaries for safe object cloning
benefits: Safe duplication of complex graph structures
Prevents infinite recursion in cyclic graphs

data_structures.description: Complex structures built by composing simpler objects rather than deep inheritance
data_structures.example: PetriNet aggregates collections of places, transitions, and arcs

model_conversion.description: Conversion functions accept variant parameter to select target format
benefits: Single entry point for all conversions
Multiple conversion strategies per format pair

model_conversion.description: Some conversions preserve enough information for round-trip transformation
model_conversion.note: Not all model types support lossless round-trip due to expressiveness differences

conformance_checking.description: Computes optimal alignment between event log traces and process model
variants: Dijkstra No Heuristics - Basic shortest path
conformance_checking.output: Alignment with synchronous/log/model moves and fitness metrics

conformance_checking.description: Replays tokens through Petri net to validate conformance
limitations: May miss certain types of conformance issues

conformance_checking.description: Conformance checking uses thread pools to parallelize trace analysis
benefits: Timeout support per trace and globally

conformance_checking.description: Traces are deduplicated by variant before processing to reduce computation
conformance_checking.benefit: Massive performance improvement on logs with many identical traces

factors.details: Implements cutting-edge process mining algorithms with complex mathematics (ILP, A*, state space exploration)
Well-organized package structure but large codebase with many modules
Consistent factory method pattern makes API approachable despite underlying complexity
Multiple representations (Petri nets, BPMN, process trees) require understanding different formalisms
Relies on scientific Python stack (numpy, pandas, scipy) but these are well-documented
Requires understanding of process mining theory, Petri net theory, and optimization algorithms

learning_curve.using_api: Medium - Factory methods provide clean interface but requires understanding process mining concepts
learning_curve.understanding_algorithms: High - State-of-the-art process mining algorithms require significant domain knowledge
learning_curve.extending: Medium-High - Consistent patterns make extension feasible but requires algorithmic expertise

code_quality.organization: Excellent - Clear package structure, consistent naming conventions
code_quality.documentation: Good - Well-documented functions with docstrings, external documentation available
code_quality.consistency: Excellent - Factory method pattern applied uniformly across all algorithms
code_quality.testability: Good - Modular design with clear interfaces
code_quality.type_hints: Good - Uses Python type hints (Union, typing module)

strengths: Comprehensive coverage of state-of-the-art process mining algorithms
Excellent algorithm organization with factory method pattern
Support for multiple process model notations (Petri nets, BPMN, process trees, DFG)
Robust event log processing with XES standard support
Parallel processing for performance on large datasets
Well-integrated with scientific Python ecosystem (pandas, numpy, scipy)
Strong academic foundation from Fraunhofer Institute
Multiple discovery algorithms (alpha, inductive, heuristic, ILP, etc.)
Visualization capabilities for all model types
Graph algorithms applicable to behavioral modeling
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license prohibits direct code reuse in proprietary projects
No permissive license option for open source reuse
Requires commercial license from PIS for closed-source use
High algorithmic complexity may be overkill for simple use cases
Steep learning curve for process mining concepts
Python performance limitations for very large event logs
No streaming processing for massive datasets
Limited error messages and debugging support
Some algorithms have high computational complexity
BPMN support is less comprehensive than Petri nets
No native UML support (would require custom implementation)

recommendations.assessment_rationale: PM4Py provides excellent algorithms and patterns for process mining that are highly relevant to UML behavioral modeling, but AGPL-3.0 license prevents direct code reuse. The library should be studied for its design patterns, algorithm concepts, and architecture, then reimplemented with clean-room development for UML-Codex.
recommendations.reuse_strategy: MUST_REBUILD - Study and reimplement, cannot lift code directly
